examples.ko: 우리 태양계는 은하계 안에 있어요.
examples.en: Our solar system is inside the galaxy.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 은하계에 관한 책을 즐겨 읽었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I have enjoyed reading books about galaxies.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 은하계를 여행하며 모험을 해요.
examples.en: The hero of the movie travels the galaxy and has adventures.

examples.ko: 은하계에는 별이 수천억 개나 있대요.
examples.en: They say there are hundreds of billions of stars in the galaxy.

examples.ko: 망원경으로 은하계 사진을 찍어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried taking a picture of the galaxy with a telescope.

examples.ko: 우리 은하계 밖에는 또 다른 은하들이 있어요.
examples.en: Outside our galaxy there are other galaxies.

explain: 과학 수업에서는 '은하'라고 짧게 말하는 일이 많아요. '은하수'는 밤하늘에 길게 보이는 별의 띠를 말할 때 써서 '은하계'와 달라요. 영화나 만화에서는 '은하계를 지키다'처럼 크고 멋있는 느낌으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I learned about galaxies in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은하계'를 짧게 줄인 말로, 수업이나 과학 글에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 은하계, used more often in science classes and writing.

phrases.example: 은하계 밖에는 또 다른 은하가 아주 많아요.
phrases.en: Outside our galaxy, there are many other galaxies.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은하계'가 우리가 사는 곳의 범위를 나타낼 때 '밖'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 밖 to talk about the space beyond our own galaxy.

phrases.en: The hero in the movie protects the galaxy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 만화에서 크고 멋있는 느낌을 줄 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in movies and comics that gives a grand, heroic feel.

explain_en: Scientific term for a galaxy, astronomy (우리가 사는 지구는 은하계 안에 있어요.) In science class people often say just '은하'. '은하수' is used for the band of stars you see across the night sky, so it differs from '은하계'. In movies and comics it appears with a grand feeling, as in '은하계를 지키다'.

t90.ax: Our solar system is inside the galaxy.

examples.ko: 박쥐는 음파를 이용해 길을 찾아요.
examples.en: Bats find their way using sound waves.

examples.ko: 음파는 물속에서도 멀리 퍼져 나가요.
examples.en: Sound waves travel far even underwater.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 음파로 물고기 떼를 찾아내요.
examples.en: This machine finds schools of fish using sound waves.

examples.ko: 소리는 음파가 되어 공기를 타고 전달돼요.
examples.en: Sound becomes sound waves and travels through the air.

examples.ko: 음파의 진동이 약해서 소리가 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: The vibration of the sound waves is weak, so I can't hear well.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 음파를 그림으로 그려 봤어요.
examples.en: In science class we drew sound waves as pictures.

explain: 소리가 퍼져 나가는 파동을 말해서 과학 수업이나 설명에서 많이 나와요. 사람이 못 듣는 높은 소리는 '초음파'라고 하고, 병원 검사에서도 들을 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '소리'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I had an ultrasound exam at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 못 듣는 높은 음파를 말하고, 병원 검사 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a high-frequency sound wave that people can't hear. It often comes up in talk about hospital exams.

phrases.en: Bats send out sound waves to find food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '음파'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 짝말로, 소리를 내보낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common verb pairing with 음파, meaning to emit a sound wave.

phrases.en: Sound waves spread in all directions through the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 설명에서 소리가 멀리 가는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in science explanations to describe sound traveling outward.

explain_en: Scientific term for the sound wave itself, as in bats' echolocation. It means the wave by which sound spreads, so it comes up mostly in science classes and explanations. Sound too high for people to hear is called '초음파' (ultrasound), which you also hear about in hospital exams. In everyday talk people simply say '소리'.

examples.ko: 햇빛이 지표면을 데우면 공기가 위로 올라가요.
examples.en: When sunlight heats the ground surface, the air rises.

examples.ko: 지표면의 온도가 평소보다 훨씬 높아요.
examples.en: The temperature of the ground surface is much higher than usual.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 지표면 아래에 물이 많이 흐른다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a lot of water flows beneath the ground surface in this area.

examples.ko: 지진이 나서 지표면 곳곳이 갈라졌어요.
examples.en: An earthquake struck and the ground surface cracked in many places.

examples.ko: 지표면에 닿는 자외선의 양이 늘었어요.
examples.en: The amount of ultraviolet light reaching the ground surface has increased.

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 하얗게 덮인 지표면이 눈부셨어요.
examples.en: After it snowed, the white-covered ground surface was dazzling.

explain: 땅의 겉면을 과학이나 지리 설명에서 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '땅바닥', '땅 표면'이라고 하고, '지면'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: When sunlight reaches the ground surface, the ground gets warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이나 열이 땅의 겉면에 이르는 것을 과학적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A scientific way to say light or heat reaches the ground's surface.

phrases.en: In summer, the ground surface temperature rises a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅 겉면의 온도를 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the temperature of the ground surface.

phrases.example: 비가 오면 땅 표면이 금방 젖어요.
phrases.en: When it rains, the surface of the ground gets wet quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지표면'과 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 지표면 but easier and more common in daily talk.

explain_en: It is used in science or geography explanations for the outer surface of the land. In daily life people say '땅바닥' or '땅 표면', and '지면' is used in a similar way.

en: to be collected; to be gathered; to be harvested

examples.ko: 현장에서 채취된 지문을 검사하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are examining the fingerprints collected at the scene.

examples.ko: 이 소금은 깨끗한 바다에서 채취돼요.
examples.en: This salt is gathered from clean seawater.

examples.ko: 약초는 아침 일찍 채취되는 것이 좋대요.
examples.en: I hear herbs are best gathered early in the morning.

examples.ko: 샘플이 채취되면 곧바로 병원으로 보내요.
examples.en: Once the sample is collected, it is sent to the hospital right away.

examples.ko: 이 버섯은 가을 산에서 많이 채취됐어요.
examples.en: A lot of these mushrooms were gathered in the autumn mountains.

examples.ko: 채취되지 않은 열매는 그냥 땅에 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The fruit that was not picked just fell to the ground.

explain: 채취되다는 '채취하다'의 결과를 말할 때 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 지문·샘플·약초 같은 물건이에요. 일상에서는 '따다', '캐다', '뽑다' 같은 말이 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The collected samples are sent to the lab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 모은 것을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something that has already been collected.

phrases.en: The fingerprints haven't been collected yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 모으지 못했다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form: not yet collected.

phrases.en: The amount of this herb that is gathered is small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼마나 모이는지 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how much is gathered.

explain_en: Passive — natural materials or samples taken out (약초가 채취되다) 채취되다 reports the outcome of 채취하다, and the subject is a thing such as a fingerprint, sample or herb, not a person. In daily talk, verbs like '따다', '캐다' and '뽑다' are more common.

t90.ax: This salt is gathered from clean seawater.

examples.ko: 강이 바다와 만나는 하구에는 새가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many birds at the river mouth where the river meets the sea.

examples.ko: 낙동강 하구에서 철새를 구경했어요.
examples.en: I watched migratory birds at the mouth of the Nakdong River.

examples.ko: 하구 근처에서는 민물과 바닷물이 섞여요.
examples.en: Near the river mouth, fresh water and sea water mix.

examples.ko: 이 하구는 갯벌이 넓어서 조개도 많이 잡혀요.
examples.en: This river mouth has wide mudflats, so lots of clams are caught.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 하구로 흙탕물이 밀려와요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, muddy water rushes toward the river mouth.

examples.ko: 강의 하구에 둑을 쌓은 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: In some places, a dam has been built at the river mouth.

explain: '강 하구'처럼 강이 바다로 들어가는 끝부분을 말해요. 강의 위쪽은 '상류', 아래쪽은 '하류'라고 해서 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 지리 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 강 하구에는 갯벌이 넓게 펼쳐져 있어요.
phrases.en: A wide tidal flat stretches out at the river mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하구'만 말해도 되지만 '강 하구'라고 하면 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can say just 하구, but 강 하구 makes it clearer.

phrases.en: I went fishing near the river mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '근처'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 근처 to give a location.

phrases.en: I walked along the river toward the river mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강의 아래쪽, 바다와 만나는 방향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to indicate the downstream direction where the river meets the sea.

explain_en: It refers to the end of a river where it flows into the sea, as in '강 하구'. The upper part of a river is '상류' and the lower part is '하류', so learn them together. You often see it in geography lessons and the news.

examples.ko: 경찰이 현장에서 지문 감식을 했어요.
examples.en: The police did a fingerprint examination at the scene.

examples.ko: 화재 원인은 감식 결과가 나와야 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can only know the cause of the fire once the forensic results come out.

examples.ko: 국과수가 증거물 감식에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The national forensic service began examining the evidence.

examples.ko: 감식이 끝나기 전까지는 현장에 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter the scene until the forensic examination is over.

examples.ko: 옛 그림은 전문가의 감식을 거쳐 진품으로 확인됐어요.
examples.en: The old painting was confirmed as genuine after an expert's appraisal.

examples.ko: 그는 골동품 감식에 평생을 바쳤어요.
examples.en: He devoted his whole life to appraising antiques.

explain: 뉴스에서는 '합동 감식'처럼 경찰이나 소방이 사고 현장을 조사할 때 많이 나와요. 미술품이나 골동품이 진짜인지 살펴볼 때도 쓰고, 이런 때는 '감정'과 가까워요. 일상 대화보다는 뉴스나 전문 분야에서 주로 써요.

phrases.en: The police and fire department began a joint forensic inspection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 기관이 함께 사고 현장을 조사할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when several agencies inspect a site together.

phrases.en: The forensic team arrived at the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감식을 맡은 팀을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the team in charge of the inspection.

phrases.en: I left the appraisal of the antique to an expert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 진짜인지 가치가 얼마인지 살필 때는 감식보다 감정을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 감정 rather than 감식 for judging whether an item is genuine or what it is worth.

explain_en: Specialist checks authenticity, as of antiques or evidence. In the news it appears in phrases like '합동 감식' (joint forensic inspection) when police or fire officials examine an accident scene. It is also used for checking whether art or antiques are genuine, which is close to '감정' (appraisal). It is used more in news and specialist fields than in casual talk.

t90.ax: He devoted his whole life to appraising antiques.

en: to rob; to extort; to seize by force

examples.ko: 강도가 가게에서 돈을 강탈했어요.
examples.en: A robber took money from the shop by force.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 이웃 나라의 땅을 강탈했어요.
examples.en: That country seized a neighboring country's land by force.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 가방을 강탈한 범인을 잡았대요.
examples.en: The news says they caught the man who snatched the bag.

examples.ko: 어린 시절의 꿈을 강탈당한 기분이었어요.
examples.en: I felt as if my childhood dream had been taken away.

examples.ko: 남의 물건을 강탈하는 것은 범죄예요.
examples.en: Taking others' belongings by force is a crime.

examples.ko: 경찰이 현금을 강탈할 계획을 막았어요.
examples.en: The police stopped a plan to rob the cash.

explain: '빼앗다'는 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '강탈하다'는 힘이나 폭력으로 억지로 빼앗을 때 쓰는 강한 말이라 뉴스나 역사 이야기에 나와요. '훔치다'는 몰래 가져가는 것이라 달라요. 피해를 입은 쪽은 '강탈당하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: He had his bag taken by force on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해를 입은 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the victim's side.

phrases.en: The robber took the customer's wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word used in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The thieves seized the villagers' property by force.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘으로 크게 빼앗는 일에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits large-scale taking by force.

explain_en: Violent forcible taking, often from a person; formal/news tone. '빼앗다' is the general word; '강탈하다' is a strong word for taking by force or violence, used in news and history. '훔치다' means taking secretly, so it differs. The victim's side uses '강탈당하다'.

t90.ax: The police stopped a plan to rob the cash.

examples.ko: 투표가 끝나면 바로 개표해요.
examples.en: As soon as voting ends, they count the votes.

examples.ko: 저녁 여덟 시부터 전국에서 개표했어요.
examples.en: Counting of the votes began across the country from eight in the evening.

examples.ko: 개표하는 동안 사람들은 텔레비전 앞에서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: While the votes were being counted, people waited in front of the TV.

examples.ko: 어제 개표한 결과가 오늘 아침에 발표됐어요.
examples.en: The results counted yesterday were announced this morning.

examples.ko: 손으로 하나하나 개표해서 시간이 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: They counted by hand one by one, so it took a long time.

examples.ko: 개표하고 나서 이긴 후보가 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: After the counting, the winning candidate gave a greeting.

explain: 개표하다는 선거에서 투표함을 열고 표를 세는 일이에요. 보통 '개표 결과', '개표 방송'처럼 선거 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 표를 넣는 일은 '투표하다', 이긴 사람이 정해지는 일은 '당선되다'예요.

phrases.en: As soon as voting ended, the vote counting began.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '개표'를 주어로 쓴 형태로, 선거 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 개표 as the subject, common in election news.

phrases.example: 저녁에 가족과 함께 개표 방송을 봤어요.
phrases.en: In the evening I watched the vote-counting broadcast with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표를 세는 과정과 결과를 알려 주는 방송이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broadcast that reports the counting process and results.

phrases.en: People are counting votes at the counting center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표를 세는 장소를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for the place where votes are counted.

explain_en: It means opening the ballot boxes and counting the votes in an election. It appears often in election news, as in '개표 결과' and '개표 방송'. Putting a vote in is 투표하다, and the winner is 당선되다.

en: opening up a port to foreigners

examples.ko: 신공항 개항이 다음 달로 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: The opening of the new airport has been pushed back to next month.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 개항이 한국에 준 영향을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, I learned about the effects the opening of ports had on Korea.

examples.ko: 개항 후에 항구 도시가 빠르게 발전했어요.
examples.en: After the port opened, the harbor city developed quickly.

examples.ko: 공항 개항 기념으로 할인 행사를 한대요.
examples.en: They say there's a discount event to celebrate the airport opening.

examples.ko: 개항 날짜가 발표되자 여행사가 바빠졌어요.
examples.en: Once the opening date was announced, travel agencies got busy.

examples.ko: 개항 이전에는 이 마을이 조용한 어촌이었어요.
examples.en: Before the port opened, this town was a quiet fishing village.

explain: 역사 시간에는 외국 배에 항구를 연 일을, 뉴스에서는 새 공항이나 항구가 처음 문을 여는 일을 말해요. 가게나 건물이 문을 여는 것은 '개점', '개관'처럼 달라요.

phrases.en: The planned opening date of the new airport was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열기로 정한 날을 뉴스처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it like in the news to talk about the scheduled opening date.

phrases.en: The opening ceremony of the new airport is held tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개항을 기념하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the ceremony celebrating the opening.

phrases.en: That airport is about to open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 문을 열 때가 가까웠다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It conveys that the opening is coming soon.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on the eve of opening

explain_en: Opening a port to foreign trade; mostly historical or news use. In history class it refers to opening a port to foreign ships, and in the news to a new airport or port opening for the first time. Shops and buildings opening use other words, such as '개점' and '개관'.

en: to be arrested; to be apprehended; to be caught

examples.ko: 도망가던 범인이 어제 검거됐어요.
examples.en: The fleeing criminal was arrested yesterday.

examples.ko: 용의자는 집 근처에서 검거됐대요.
examples.en: They say the suspect was arrested near his home.

examples.ko: 검거된 사람들은 모두 조사를 받았어요.
examples.en: All the people who were arrested were questioned.

examples.ko: 범인이 검거되자 사람들이 안심했어요.
examples.en: People felt relieved when the criminal was arrested.

examples.ko: 범인이 이렇게 빨리 검거되는 경우는 드물어요.
examples.en: It is rare for a criminal to be arrested this fast.

examples.ko: 검거될 때까지 그는 이름을 숨기고 살았어요.
examples.en: He lived hiding his name until he was arrested.

explain: '잡히다'는 누구에게나 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '검거되다'는 경찰이 범인을 붙잡을 때 뉴스에서 써요. 비슷한 '체포되다'는 법적 절차의 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: The police arrested the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검거되다'는 잡히는 쪽, '검거하다'는 잡는 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '검거하다' is from the side that catches; '검거되다' is from the side that gets caught.

phrases.en: The thief was caught soon after.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검거되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '검거되다' and more natural in daily talk.

phrases.en: He was arrested last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법적 절차로 붙잡힌다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of being taken in through legal procedure.

explain_en: Passive, news style: a criminal gets caught by police. '잡히다' is an everyday word for anyone, while '검거되다' is the news word for a criminal being caught by the police. The similar '체포되다' feels more like a formal legal procedure.

dis.h: be caught by police, news style

p.n: 검거되다 is the police catching a suspect, a news-style word; 체포되다 is the formal legal arrest.

t90.ax: The fleeing criminal was arrested yesterday.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 아주 작은 균의 검출이 가능해요.
examples.en: This machine can detect even very tiny germs.

examples.ko: 검출 결과는 내일 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll let you know the test results tomorrow.

examples.ko: 검출을 쉽게 하려고 물에 색을 넣었어요.
examples.en: We added color to the water to make detection easier.

examples.ko: 새 프로그램은 오류 검출 속도가 훨씬 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: The new program is much faster at detecting errors.

examples.ko: 화재 때 연기 검출은 센서가 맡아요.
examples.en: In a fire, a sensor handles the smoke detection.

examples.ko: 검출에 실패해서 어제 다시 검사했어요.
examples.en: Detection failed, so we tested again yesterday.

explain: '찾아내다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '검출'은 기계나 검사 방법으로 어떤 것이 있는지 확인해 낼 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '성분이 검출되다'처럼 동사 '검출되다'로 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Bacteria were detected in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 이 동사형을 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This verb form is the one used most in the news.

phrases.example: 이 검사는 아주 작은 성분도 검출해요.
phrases.en: This test detects even tiny components.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사하는 쪽이 찾아낼 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the tester as the subject.

phrases.en: Detection standards differ by country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 정도부터 있다고 보는지 정한 기준을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the standard for deciding something is present.

explain_en: Finding a substance in a test or inspection (세균 검출) 찾아내다 is the everyday word; 검출 is for confirming through a machine or test that something is present. In the news the verb form appears more often, as in '성분이 검출되다'.

t90.ax: I'll let you know the test results tomorrow.

en: to shoot down; to bring down

examples.ko: 군인들이 적의 비행기를 격추했어요.
examples.en: The soldiers shot down an enemy plane.

examples.ko: 방어 시스템이 날아오는 드론을 격추할 거예요.
examples.en: The defense system will shoot down the incoming drone.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 전투기를 격추한 사건을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a news report about the incident in which a fighter jet was shot down.

examples.ko: 게임에서 적 비행기를 다 격추하고 점수를 얻었어요.
examples.en: In the game, I shot down all the enemy planes and earned points.

examples.ko: 적을 격추해야 다음 단계로 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to shoot down the enemy to move on to the next level.

examples.ko: 비행기를 격추하는 장면이 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: A scene of a plane being shot down appears in the movie.

explain: '쏘다'는 총이나 미사일을 쏘는 행동이고, '격추하다'는 날아다니는 비행기나 드론을 쏴서 떨어뜨리는 결과까지 나타내요. 목적어는 비행기, 드론처럼 하늘에 떠 있는 것만 와요. 뉴스와 게임에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: The plane was shot down by a missile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨어지는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요. 주어는 비행기나 드론이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of what falls; the subject is a plane or drone.

phrases.en: The fighter jet shot down the enemy drone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격추하다'와 뜻이 같고, 뉴스에서 같이 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 격추하다; also common in news.

phrases.en: The soldier shot down the incoming drone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격추하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이라 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say 격추하다; more natural in everyday speech.

explain_en: '쏘다' (to shoot) is the act of firing, while '격추하다' also includes the result: the target is brought down. The object is always something in the air, such as a plane or a drone. You hear it often in the news and in games.

examples.ko: 경찰은 공격자의 얼굴을 확인했어요.
examples.en: The police checked the attacker's face.

examples.ko: 해킹 공격자가 회사 서버에 몰래 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A hacker secretly got into the company server.

examples.ko: 먼저 때린 사람이 공격자로 알려졌어요.
examples.en: The person who hit first was identified as the attacker.

examples.ko: 공격자는 도망가면서 가방을 던졌어요.
examples.en: The attacker threw a bag while running away.

examples.ko: 게임에서 공격자 역할은 빨리 움직여야 해요.
examples.en: In the game, the attacker role has to move fast.

examples.ko: 이번 사고의 공격자를 아직 찾지 못했어요.
examples.en: We have not yet found the attacker in this incident.

explain: 축구나 농구에서 공격하는 선수는 보통 '공격수'라고 해요. 공격자는 사건이나 해킹, 게임에서 공격하는 쪽을 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. 반대쪽은 사건에서는 '피해자', 게임이나 스포츠에서는 '수비수'를 써요.

phrases.en: The police caught the attacker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in crime news.

phrases.en: The attacker and the victim did not know each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건에서 두 사람을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name both sides in an incident.

phrases.en: In the game, the attacking side starts first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임에서 공격하는 편을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the attacking side in a game.

explain_en: General person who attacks, in sports, war or crime; more formal/neutral. In soccer or basketball, the player who attacks is usually called 공격수. 공격자 fits better for an incident, hacking, or a game role. The other side is 피해자 in an incident, and 수비수 in sports or games.

t90.ax: The police checked the attacker's face.

en: to announce; to make public; to promulgate

examples.ko: 정부가 새 정책을 공표했어요.
examples.en: The government officially announced the new policy.

examples.ko: 시험 결과는 다음 주에 공표할 거예요.
examples.en: The exam results will be made public next week.

examples.ko: 회사는 계획을 공표하기 전에 직원에게 먼저 알렸어요.
examples.en: The company told employees first before announcing the plan publicly.

examples.ko: 공표하는 날까지 비밀을 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: You must keep it secret until the day it is announced.

examples.ko: 연구 결과를 공표하면 사람들이 관심을 가져요.
examples.en: When research results are made public, people take an interest.

examples.ko: 선거 결과를 공표해서 모두 알게 되었어요.
examples.en: They announced the election results, so everyone found out.

explain: '발표하다'는 학교에서 과제를 말할 때도 쓰지만, '공표하다'는 정부·기관이 법이나 결과를 공식적으로 세상에 알릴 때만 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The new law will be made public tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알려지는 내용을 주어로 말할 때 써요. 법이나 결과와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the announced content is the subject. Fits laws and results.

phrases.en: The government postponed announcing the results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 알리는 일을 뒤로 늦출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the official announcement is put off until later.

phrases.en: The announcement date hasn't been set yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 발표가 언제인지 말할 때 '날짜'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 날짜 to talk about when the official announcement happens.

explain_en: Officially make policy or results public; formal, government. '발표하다' can be used even for presenting homework at school, but '공표하다' is only for a government or institution officially announcing laws or results to the public. It is rarely used in everyday talk.

dis.h: officially make results or policy public
gh: notify members or staff of an update
solemnly proclaim, like a leader declaring

p.n: 공표 is official publication to the public; 공지 is a notice to a group.

t90.ax: The exam results will be made public next week.
